claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 initially exists in a high-temperature disordered BCC state.
During cooling, the disordered BCC phase enters a miscibility gap.
The alloy first undergoes spinodal decomposition into Ni–Al-lean BCC1 and Ni–Al-rich BCC2 regions.
Below an ordering transition temperature, the Ni–Al-rich BCC2 regions order into B2.
Sequential spinodal decomposition and ordering produce a hierarchical reciprocal BCC/B2 microstructure.
The resulting microstructure contains a Ni–Al-lean BCC matrix interspersed with Ni–Al-rich ordered B2 nanoparticles.
Larger B2 particles may contain embedded Ni–Al-lean BCC nanoparticles.
Minor FCC phases, including grain-boundary Widmanstätten side-plates, may be present.
Sequential decomposition and ordering establish chemical partitioning and phase boundaries that refine the microstructure.
The hierarchical BCC/B2 features obstruct dislocation motion.
Obstruction of dislocation motion by the BCC/B2 microstructure increases hardness.
The 1100 °C annealed-and-quenched condition has a near-equal BCC/FCC phase mixture.
The 1100 °C annealed-and-quenched condition has the lowest measured hardness.
The 1100 °C baseline represents an undecomposed high-temperature BCC state prior to significant spinodal decomposition and ordering.
Relative to the 1100 °C baseline, quenching from 1200 °C and especially 1300 °C will produce a larger BCC fraction.
Relative to the 1100 °C baseline, quenching from 1200 °C and especially 1300 °C will produce a more pronounced spinodal-decomposition signature and a higher density of ordered B2 precipitates.
Specimens quenched from 1200 °C and 1300 °C will have higher hardness than the 1100 °C baseline.
The proposed mechanism applies within 1100–1300 °C under argon when rapid water quenching freezes in the sequential decomposition and ordering features.
The mechanism may not apply outside 1100–1300 °C or at cooling rates too slow to preserve the proposed microstructure.

contradictions.description: The 1100 °C baseline is described both as a near-equal BCC/FCC mixture and as an undecomposed high-temperature BCC state. A substantial FCC fraction is inconsistent with treating that same state as undecomposed single-phase BCC without further qualification.
